title: Token Reconciler — compact attribution ledger & export patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Design a compact, reconciler-focused token-level ledger component and export patterns for the Redwood Console cost views. The goal is a scannable, exportable UI that helps engineering and finance teams reconcile billed token costs to application events (routes, prompts, roles). This ticket covers the UI/interaction patterns, prototype flows for CSV/NDJSON export schemas, and a small set of pricing controls (preset slabs + custom allocation tags).

Scope:
- Compact attribution ledger (tile + row hybrid) that surfaces per-request token counts, model variant, quantization profile, route tag, actor/role, and applied price-per-token.
- Reconciliation metadata: unique recon_id per export row, hash fingerprint for prompt fingerprinting, and normalized deltas when price changes occur.
- Export formats: CSV (human-friendly) and NDJSON (line-item for ingestion). Export must include allocation tags and rollback metadata.
- Pricing UI patterns: slab picker, tier visualizer, and per-route override quick-actions.
- UX flows for role-aware allocation (e.g., split cost between system vs. end-user tokens), and manual reallocation for disputed lines.

Trade-offs & constraints:
- Layout needs to remain readable with tens of thousands of lines — we use virtualized rows + compact sparklines; full row expansion reveals full prompt text/metadata.
- Export performance: prototype suggests server-side streaming for NDJSON; engineering prefers paginated exports for CSV to avoid timeouts. Need to reconcile expectation.
- Pricing complexity: avoid surface-level exposure to fractional micro-pricing in the main ledger; expose advanced fields under an "allocation detail" flyout.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) High-fidelity prototype (desktop, tablet) with row / tile hybrid and expansion state.
2) Export schema documented (CSV sample + NDJSON schema), with example export file in Drive.
3) Pricing patterns documented with visual language and a small component library: slab picker, override pill, allocation flyout.
4) PM + Eng sign-off on performance and export approach (streaming vs. pagination).
5) Accessibility: ledger rows keyboard-focusable; exports reachable through keyboard and screen reader labels.

Design decisions so far:
- Use compact 4-line row with left-aligned route tag, center token counters (user/system/total), right-aligned price + delta chip. Expanded rows surface prompt fingerprint and full prompt text.
- Introduce a condensed "recon timeline" sparkline column that encodes cost drift during the selected date range.
- Exports include a recon_id (uuid), event_timestamp (ISO8601), route, model_variant, token_user, token_system, token_total, price_per_token_usd, allocation_tags (semicolon-separated), recon_notes. NDJSON lines mirror the CSV headers but preserve nested metadata in a separate JSON-encoded field called "meta_blob".

Open questions:
- Should allocation_tags be free-text or a controlled taxonomy? (PM leaning: taxonomy)
- How to present refunds or credit events in the same ledger without overwhelming the primary cost rows? Proposed: muted rows with a credit icon and ability to filter them out.

Deliverables linked in attachments. Prototype URL contains V1 and V2 mockups — V2 adds a lightweight reconciliation modal with manual split controls.

Export button labeled with aria-describedby that explains formats
Color contrast for chip deltas must meet AA
Keyboard flow documented in component spec
